title: Capacity shepherding and incident-aware rollout timeline (Nov 2026) - draft
content:
Overview:
This doc captures a capacity-first, incident-aware rollout strategy for the upcoming 11/2026 release. The emphasis is on 'shepherding' — small incremental traffic ramps paired with active telemetry gates and pre-scheduled mitigation steps. This is a working timeline intended for Release Engineering + SRE + Serving-runtime leads.

Why this is different: 
- We treat capacity as a first-class signal (not just error/latency). 
- Rollout adjusts to observed KV cache hit rates, batch sizes, and GPU queue depth per zone.
- Automated throttles are enabled that will reduce new session acceptance if p95 latency or CPU/GPU queue depth exceed thresholds.

Quick summary (release notes draft snippet):
- Serving runtime: adaptive kernel selection for long-context attention (reduces steady-state p99 latency by ~8% in internal benchmarks).
- Optimize: batching suggestion engine added to the Console (alpha).
- Private: installer fixes for single-tenant KMS rotation (minor).
- Observability: per-model warmup trace added to rollout traces.
Known issues: cold-starts in new regions may show elevated 5xx on first 10–20 requests; warmup hook added but not fully mitigated.

Pre-launch checklist (owners listed):
- [ ] Release manifest final (owner: Marcus Chen) — include model versions, kernel flags, quantized builds.
- [ ] Canary package deployed to staging cluster and smoke test passing (owner: Asha Pillai).
- [ ] KV prefix caching enabled and validated (owner: Diego Morales).
- [ ] Autoscaler soft caps reviewed for Dedicated pools (owner: Leah O'Keefe).
- [ ] Hooks for rollback autopolicy tested in dry-run (owner: eng-release-engineering oncall).
- [ ] Notify Customer Success + Product with impact summary and FAQ (owner: release-ops).
- [ ] Create escalation Slack channel: #release-2026-11-shepherd (owner: Marcus Chen).

Release-day incident-aware ramp schedule (all times UTC):
Day 0 — Dark launch + validation
  2026-11-02 09:00 — Dark launch 0.5% global traffic, max 50 qps per region. (Telemetry: request-sampling=100%, tracing=on).
  2026-11-02 09:15 — Verify core smoke tests (generation correctness, function calling). Check: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, GPU queue depth, KV hit rate.
  2026-11-02 10:00 — If all gates green, hold for 6 hours of steady-state metrics; otherwise rollback to prev variant.

Day 1 — Controlled ramp with capacity shepherding
  2026-11-03 09:00 — Ramp to 5% traffic. Circuit: region-level admission control enabled with per-zone capacity tokens.
  2026-11-03 12:00 — Crash check + manual inspection by shepherd: Diego Morales.
  2026-11-03 18:00 — Ramp to 12% if: p95 latency <= +15% baseline AND 5xx < 0.5% AND GPU queuing < 70% of soft-cap.

Day 2 — Burst cohort and L7 gating
  2026-11-04 09:00 — Add burst cohort: allow spikes (up to +2x qps) for 10 minute windows to observe autoscaler response.
  2026-11-04 13:00 — Enable L7 route-level fallback to smaller model-variant for latency-sensitive routes (auto-fallback config id: rb-fallback-11-26).
  2026-11-04 20:00 — If any region sees p95 > +25% baseline OR 5xx > 1.5% for 15m, initiate automatic throttle to 30% of new sessions in that region and paging.

Day 3 — Regional expansion and DDR (de-risk, defer, reroute)
  2026-11-05 09:00 — Expand to 40% global traffic, but cap new sessions per region to precomputed capacity budgets.
  2026-11-05 12:00 — SRE heatmap review: Leah O'Keefe and eng-sre oncall to validate telemetry signals.
  2026-11-05 18:00 — If all green, schedule final ramp next day.

Day 4 — Final ramp to GA
  2026-11-06 10:00 — Ramp to 75% traffic. Check model quality regression tests (A/B evaluation set).
  2026-11-06 16:00 — Ramp to 100% if no regressions: baseline token-cost within +/-5% and user-facing latency within SLOs.

Rollback & mitigation playbook (quick reference):
- Immediate rollback trigger: sustained 5xx > 2% for 10 minutes OR p99 latency > 3x baseline for 5 minutes.
- Partial rollback: region-only rollback or switch to fallback model-variant for latency-sensitive routes.
- Throttle: reduce new session acceptance by 50% in affected region(s) and enable request-shaping.
- Hotfix path: if fix < 30min, patch and canary to 1% then re-evaluate; else rollback full and schedule hotfix release window.

Telemetry & gates (what to watch):
- Error budget burn (per-route and global) — threshold 15% of daily budget consumed triggers human review.
- p50/p95/p99 latency buckets — compare to 7-day baseline.
- 5xx and 429 rates — per-route and per-region.
- GPU queue depth and average batch size — watch for sudden drops in batch size (indicates traffic fragmentation).
- KV cache hit rate and warmup traces — new regions should reach >80% within 30m of ramp.
- Model output quality checks — run 1000 eval prompts against canary and compare embedding similarity and token divergence metrics.

Rollout communications & stakeholder notes:
- Push a slim release note to #platform-updates at each ramp milestone (owner: Marcus Chen).
- Customer impact list for CS: top 12 customers with Dedicated contracts (attach known region mapping).
- Product: note feature gating for Console alpha features (batching suggestion engine).

Housekeeping commands & scripts (ops shortcuts):
- Dry-run rollback: infra/cli rollback --release=2026-11-shepherd --dry-run
- Throttle enable: infra/cli throttle --region=eu-west1 --pct=30 --reason="p95-exceeded"
- Warmup run: infra/cli warmup --region=ap-southeast1 --model=baseline-11-2026 --concurrency=20 --duration=900
- Trace link pattern: https://tracing.redwood-infra/runs/{{run_id}}

Escalation matrix:
- Triage first 15m: oncall-release (pager) -> release-eng lead (Marcus Chen) -> SRE lead (Leah O'Keefe)
- Pager channel: #pager-release (auto-forward to mobile oncall)
- Secondary: #release-2026-11-shepherd (chat + ops)

After-action items (post-GA 30d):
- Run cost delta analysis per model and region (owner: product-analytics).
- Collect quality regressions and tie to model flip decisions (owner: applied-ml).
- Telemetry cliff analysis: identify first 30m anomalies in new regions and propose warmup improvements.

Draft release notes (for internal review):
Title: "Nov 2026 — Serving runtime & Console optimizations"
Highlights:
- Adaptive attention kernel selection lowered median latency on long-context workloads and improved throughput on T4-like hardware.
- Console: early alpha for batching suggestion engine to help customers reduce per-token cost at low latency.
- Private: installer KMS rotation fixes and CLI flags for on-prem deployment stability.
- Observability: rollout warmup traces and per-model cold-start telemetry.
Impact: incremental perf wins for production workloads; short-lived cold-start noise in some new regions expected.
Action for customers: None required. For Dedicated customers we will email a note with planned maintenance windows if their reserved pools receive the new variant.

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Should we enable client-side retry hints during first 24 hours? Pros: reduce user-facing errors. Cons: can mask real capacity issues. (owner: Product + Eng SRE)
- Fine-tune GPU queue depth throttle thresholds per instance type (owner: infra/perf).
- Add an automated ticket creation for any rollbacks that last > 30 minutes with diagnostic logs attached (owner: release-tooling).

Notes to self: this doc is intentionally conservative on ramp pacing; we can compress if early telemetry is very healthy, but prefer multiple small ramps with shepherd checks.

-- End of draft --
